data.title: Huang returns as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervention in abrupt board reversal
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump says Huang's return poses no national security risk
  • Board launches probe into possible foreign intelligence efforts targeting Huang
  • Huang's comeback underscores Nvidia's deep dependence on influential co-founder
  • Nvidia shares close up 31.5%

By Deborah Mary Sophia, Anhata Rooprai and David Morgan

Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday under pressure from US President Donald Trump, a stunning reversal following his resignation over revelations of extramarital affairs, drawing approval from Wall Street and opposition from US lawmakers.

Huang's comeback caps a whirlwind week of events that roiled markets and tore through the AI ecosystem that has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout.

But the board's about-face — less than a week after Chair Harvey Jones said Nvidia would not rehire Huang as CEO because his personal behavior was inconsistent with the company's code of conduct — raises questions about its independence, governance experts said, even as the company's investigation remains unfinished.

Huang's comeback boosted Wall Street and sent Nvidia's shares soaring. The stock closed up 31.5%, adding nearly $1 trillion in market value, vaulting the chipmaker back to the position of the second-biggest company by market value after Apple . The gains were not enough, however, to erase all losses since Huang's resignation on November 12.

Nvidia said in a statement that based on US government input the board was confident that "Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk," a claim backed by Trump in an interview with CNBC.

Huang said in a statement that he was honored to return and "can’t wait to get back to work.” He returned to company headquarters to cheers from employees and said he was going to "be a better CEO the second time around," Business Insider reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.

"Jensen's return is not a total shock, but it does send a troubling message about the state of corporate governance in America," said James St. Aubin, chief investment officer at Ocean Park Asset Management. "Certain executives are going to be held to different standards if you are perceived to be a one of one," he said, adding Huang would still have to answer "some tough questions from Congress."

Lawmakers across party lines strongly objected to Huang's reinstatement and called on Congress to pass the Chip Security Act, a bill that seeks to stop legally exported advanced chips from being diverted to China, where their sales are restricted.

US Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Trump was "putting his own financial interests ... before our national security," while Senator Pete Ricketts, a Nebraska Republican, said Huang's return "doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips."

TRUMP'S SUPPORT FOR HUANG

Huang returned at the strong urging of Trump, industry leaders including Elon Musk, and some investors. His departure had reverberated from Silicon Valley to Taipei. A petition calling for his reinstatement drew more than 180,000 signatures, underscoring the unusually strong support for an executive who stepped down amid controversy.

"I believe my intervention was very important to get Jensen Huang back," Trump told CNBC.

Trump owns between $11 million and $55 million in Nvidia stock, according to a Reuters review of his annual financial disclosure for 2025 and share trading disclosures for 2026. Monday’s surge in Nvidia shares could have boosted Trump's net worth by as much as $17 million. A White House spokesperson said Trump’s stock and bond portfolio was independently managed by third-party financial institutions and neither the president nor any member of his family had any ability to direct or influence how the portfolio was invested.

Nvidia's board did not mention Huang's affairs. Apart from Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman who is accused of having ties with Beijing, Huang is accused of having had intimate relationships with at least two Nvidia employees.

Jensen Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologized, but has not publicly addressed the individual alleged relationships in detail. China has denied the espionage allegations. Attempts by Reuters to reach Alice Huang have been unsuccessful.

"There were definitely a lot of people who wanted him back. The extent that the administration intervened, the extent that shareholders intervened, it will be impossible to know," said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers. "But it tells us to some extent that Jensen Huang was too big to be fired."

CHINA IS KEY TO NVIDIA

The moves come as Nvidia faces heightened scrutiny in Washington over the flow of advanced AI chips to China. US authorities have tightened licensing rules for some chip shipments and overseas data centers serving Chinese companies, while lawmakers are preparing to question Huang, who has pushed for greater access to the Chinese market.

Huang has agreed to testify before the US Senate in a public hearing on December 3, the Senate Banking Committee said. Huang's personal spokesperson declined to comment.

Trump told CNBC that he had urged Nvidia to continue reviewing its compliance with US export controls to ensure it was adequately protecting national security. Trump, who visited Shenzhen last week, told CNBC he had spoken to Chinese President Xi Jinping about Huang.

Huang's exit from Nvidia threatened its business in China, Reuters reported on Monday, with some customers there cancelling or hesitating to place orders, jeopardizing billions in revenue.

The US on Monday was set to add Singapore-based chip firm Megaspeed, which is closely tied to an espionage investigation involving Nvidia, to its trade blacklist, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters.

The Nvidia board has formed a committee to investigate whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted Huang and another committee focused on national security and export controls.

The company is also facing multiple investigations over issues ranging from potential accounting irregularities to suspected chip smuggling, and a shareholder lawsuit accusing the company and Huang of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang's relationship with Alice Huang.

data.title: Stock market holiday today: BSE, NSE to remain closed for Guru Nanak Jayanti
data.description:
Indian stock markets will remain closed today, November 24, on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev (Guru Nanak Jayanti), with trading suspended across major segments on both the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Trading in equities, equity derivatives, securities lending and borrowing (SLBs), currency derivatives, and interest rate derivatives will remain shut for the day on both exchanges.

Meanwhile, the commodity derivatives segment will remain closed during the morning session from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, but trading will resume in the evening session between 5:00 pm and 11:30 pm/11:55 pm.

Market activity on the NSE and BSE will resume on November 25 (Wednesday).

Indian equity benchmarks snapped their two-day winning streak and ended lower on November 23, with the Nifty falling 1.7 percent, marking its biggest single-day decline in nearly five months. Broad-based selling in auto, metal and financial stocks dragged the benchmarks lower.

At close, the Sensex was down 1,483.72 points or 1.77 percent at 82,435.99, and the Nifty was down 450.95 points or 1.75 percent at 25,349.65.

Biggest Nifty losers were Tata Steel, Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, Hindalco, HDFC Bank, while gainers included TCS, Tech Mahindra, Shriram Finance, HCL Technologies, Titan Company.

On the sectoral front, except Information Technology and Consumer Durables, all other sectoral indices ended in the red Metal, Oil & Gas, PSU Bank, Private Bank, Infra, Energy, Auto down 1-3 percent.

The broader markets outperformed the benchmark indices, with the Nifty Midcap index falling 0.7 percent, while the Nifty Smallcap index losing 0.66%.

"Markets witnessed sharp profit-booking on Monday, declining over 1.5%, following the recent four-week rally. After an initial uptick, the benchmark indices gradually drifted lower as the session progressed and eventually settled near the day’s lows on the monthly expiry day. The Nifty closed around 25,349, while the Sensex settled at 82,435.99, reflecting a broad-based deterioration in market sentiment," said Ajit Mishra, SVP – Research, Religare Broking.

"Sentiment remained subdued amid a sharp sell-off across global markets, particularly in US and Asian technology stocks, driven by concerns over AI-related valuations, the US interest-rate outlook and rising global risk aversion. Despite the correction, the broader domestic market backdrop continues to draw support from strong foreign investor inflows, which have exceeded USD 13 billion so far in November. Brent crude remained below USD92 per barrel, while the rupee opened stronger against the US dollar, providing some macroeconomic relief," Mishra added.

"The Nifty witnessed profit-booking after coming close to retesting the 26,000 mark and is likely to find support in the 25,000–25,300 zone. On the upside, the 25,650–25,800 zone is likely to act as an immediate resistance band. We recommend avoiding aggressive fresh exposure amid heightened volatility and using the possible consolidation to selectively accumulate quality stocks."

"From a sectoral perspective, banking and financials may take a breather following their sharp rally, while other rate-sensitive sectors such as auto and realty are likely to continue offering buying opportunities, alongside the pharma and healthcare basket," he added.

On Monday, the Indian rupee snapped its five-day winning streak and ended lower by 24 paise at 92.91 against the US dollar on Monday, compared with the previous session's close of 92.67.

"The rupee witnessed minor profit booking, declining around 30 paise to 92.90, as selling pressure emerged in the secondary equity market. Despite the correction, the broader currency trend remains supported by sustained foreign fund inflows, even with the Dollar Index near 103.80 and crude oil around $90," said Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities.

"Market participants will closely track FII activity this week, particularly after cumulative inflows of over ₹1 lakh crore, to assess whether foreign buying momentum continues into the final week of November. Going ahead, the rupee is expected to trade in a range of 92.50–93.55, with fund flows remaining a key driver," he added.

data.title: China Stock Market May See Additional Support On Tuesday
data.description:
BEIJING (dpa-AFX) - The China stock market on Monday snapped the two-day slide in which it had fallen more than 50 points or 1.4 percent. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just beneath the 3,540-point plateau and it may extend its gains on Tuesday.

The global forecast for the Asian markets is broadly positive thanks to easing oil prices and a sharp rebound among technology stocks. The European and U.S. markets were sharply higher and the Asian bourses are expected to follow that lead.

The SCI finished slightly higher on Monday as gains from the financials and manufacturers were offset by weakness among the technology, energy and manufacturing companies.

For the day, the index rose 5.16 points or 0.15 percent to finish at 3,538.95 after trading between 3,476.65 and 3,544.60. The Shenzhen Composite Index gained 44.92 points or 2.33 percent to end at 1,969.82.

The lead from Wall Street is solid as the major averages opened sharply higher on Monday and remained firmly in the green throughout the trading day, ending near session highs.

The Dow spiked 1,447.98 points or 3.01 percent to finish at 49,595.31, while the NASDAQ surged 1,471.83 points or 6.51 percent to close at 24,089.56 and the S&P 500 rallied 326.78 points or 4.73 percent to end at 7,237.17.

The rally on Wall Street came as traders looked to pick up stocks at reduced levels following the recent weakness, which dragged the major averages down to their lowest closing levels in seven months.

AI giant Nvidia (NVDA) fueled the rally after the company announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board.

Semiconductor stocks also showed a substantial move back to the upside, while computer hardware stocks, gold, networking and airline stocks also saw significant strength.

Crude oil prices tumbled on Monday as U.S.-Iran re-escalation concerns eased after U.S. President Donald Trump said he has put off plans to attack Iran until January 1. West Texas Intermediate crude for January delivery was down $3.43 or 4.11 percent at $79.98 per barrel.

data.title: Huang's Return Removes Largest Overhang on Nvidia — Market Talk
data.description: Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO removes the largest overhang on the stock, say analysts at Yorkville Ives in a note. The brokerage maintains an outperform rating and $225 target price on Nvidia but sees scope for the target to rise to $300 with Huang's return. "The gap between $225 and $300 is the value of Jensen with the governance questions behind him." The closing of the independent committee's investigation on foreign intelligence efforts, a clean read on the export probe, and a 4Q print delivered by a CEO whose tenure is no longer a topic on the earnings call could be critical for the revaluation of the stock, they say. Nvidia shares last closed 31.5% higher at $165.05. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)

data.title: Australian shares jump as Huang's Nvidia return boosts risk sentiment
data.description:
Australian shares rose more than 1% on Tuesday and were headed for their biggest daily gain in nearly three weeks, as index heavyweight miners and banks advanced, while a sharp rally in Nvidia boosted risk appetite globally.

The S&P/ASX 200 index rose 1.4% to 8,689.60 by 2320 GMT and was on track for its largest one-day gain since November 5. The benchmark slipped 0.3% on Monday to its lowest close since May 20.

Resources stocks climbed 1.7%, tracking a surge in copper prices after Nvidia moved to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO in a dramatic reversal. Copper is widely used in data-centre infrastructure.

Mining heavyweights BHP and Rio Tinto gained 2.2% and 2.4%, respectively.

Huang's comeback capped a whirlwind week of events that had roiled markets and torn through the AI ecosystem that has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout.

Nvidia's 31% surge boosted Wall Street overnight, helping lift risk appetite across global equities, including Australia.

In Sydney, gold stocks advanced as bullion prices recovered from last week's 9% slide. Northern Star Resources and Evolution Mining gained 1.9% and 4.6%, respectively.

Technology stocks , which declined roughly 5.5% over the last two sessions, jumped 3.5%. Logistics software maker WiseTech Global and accounting software firm Xero climbed 3.8% and 4.5%, respectively.

Banks advanced 1%, putting the sector on track to snap a five-session losing streak. The "Big Four" lenders rose between 0.4% and 0.8%.

Real estate stocks (.AXRE) jumped 2.1%, while the healthcare sub-index surged 1.8%.

Investors now await monthly inflation data due on Wednesday for clues on the Reserve Bank of Australia's policy outlook ahead of its final board meeting of the year in December.

In New Zealand, the benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index rose 2.1% to 14,023.03, recovering from a 2.7% drop on Monday.

data.title: Japan's Nikkei rises over 4% after Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO
data.description:
By Satoshi Sugiyama

Japan's Nikkei share average climbed more than 4% on Tuesday, tracking a sharp rally on Wall Street as Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO rekindled investor enthusiasm for the AI trade.

The Nikkei 225 Index advanced 4.62% to 59,045.30, rebounding from a 5% slump on Friday. The broader Topix climbed 2.8% to 3,777.21, reversing a nearly 4% drop posted on Friday. Tokyo markets were closed on Monday for a public holiday.

"Such positive news has provided a good pretext for buying back shares. Because the market had fallen so sharply, the short-covering rebound is also proving large," said Masahiro Ichikawa, chief market strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui DS Asset Management.

AI- and chip-related shares led the Nikkei's rally, with Murata Manufacturing jumping 14.6%, Advantest rising 13.2% and Tokyo Electron surging 11.4%. Data-centre suppliers such as Furukawa Electric advanced 13.15% and Mitsui Kinzoku gained 9.33%.

The market breadth was positive, with 158 advancers on the Nikkei index against 64 decliners, while 3 stocks were flat.

Shares of Nvidia , a bellwether for the AI sector, surged 31.5% overnight in their biggest one-day percentage gain since May 9, 2003.

The chipmaker had announced Huang's resignation on November 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy, a development that helped trigger last week's global equity selloff.

At the same time, analysts say Huang's return does not mean uncertainties surrounding restrictions on data-centre construction will be eased, nor does it improve the profitability of AI investment.

"Uncertainty has actually increased over how much tighter restrictions on China could become going forward," said Shingo Ide, chief equity strategist at NLI Research Institute.

"Whether it's restrictions on data-centre construction or export controls on China, these issues could drag on for six months to a year. During that time, the market will likely swing back and forth on comments from key officials and various headlines."

data.title: Wall Street analysts scramble to upgrade Nvidia’s stock after Huang’s return
data.description:
Nvidia reinstated former CEO Jensen Huang on Monday, leading several Wall Street analysts to turn more bullish on the stock.

  • Melius Research upgraded the dominant maker of artificial intelligence semiconductors to buy from hold, and put a $220 price target on the stock, implying roughly 75% upside from Nvidia's Friday close.
  • Bernstein did the same, raising Nvidia to outperform from market perform and putting a $200 price target on the stock that would equal a 59% advance.
  • StoneX upgraded Nvidia to buy from hold and set a $270 price target on shares. The new target suggests 115% upside from Friday's close.
  • Oppenheimer also elevated its stock rating to outperform from perform. Its $250 target on the shares is 99% higher than Nvidia's last closing price.
  • Citigroup reiterated a buy recommendation and lifted its price target on Nvidia shares to $240 from $225 — 91% above the last close.

"Jensen's return is a win for AI and a win for investors," Oppenheimer analyst Rick Schafer said Monday in a note to clients.

With his return "long-term concerns we had are significantly alleviated," Ben Reitzes, an analyst at Melius Research, wrote in a report Monday. "While not out of the woods in terms of investigations, accounting investigations and political theater — no one is more focused than Jensen."

Shares of Nvidia soared as much as 37% on Monday after the board, at the urging of President Donald Trump, announced the unexpected return of Huang, the company's 63-year-old co-founder and longtime chief executive.

Huang stepped down from Nvidia on Nov. 12, after reports of several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. Through Friday, Nvidia shares had tumbled 28% since Huang's departure, underscoring investor misgivings toward Nvidia's management succession and questions over Huang's reputation as a top dealmaker in the AI supply chain.

Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon noted that Huang's reinstatement should inspire confidence in Nvidia's ability to grow near term, but it doesn't mean the company is completely out of the woods either.

"As we remain positive on AI buildout fundamentals, and with Jensen back in the seat, we upgrade today back to [outperform] (as his exit was the primary reason for the downgrade)," Rasgon wrote in a report Monday. "That being said, this whole mess has brought up some legitimate questions and will leave some overhangs in place that may limit NVDA's multiple for now."

Reitzes at Melius was less circumspect, saying Huang could take several steps to mitigate concerns regarding succession and corporate compliance.

"The 'new Jensen' should quickly address investor concerns around how they conduct and manage circular deals, the real amount of sales to neoclouds that inevitably serve China, how compliance will go from here and what a real succession plan looks like," Reitzes wrote.

Bernstein and Melius Research's calls match the consensus on Wall Street, where 48 of 65 analysts rate Nvidia a buy or strong buy, LSEG data shows.

data.title: Morgan Stanley says this is a big buying opportunity: ‘We’re not going to miss it’
data.description:
Friday's selloff, led by tech and AI-related stocks, reflected investor concern around artificial spending — whether it might slow and would it be profitable. The retreat also gave "a clearer capitulation signal," and was what Morgan Stanley said the firm had been waiting for.

"This is the fat pitch we have patiently been waiting for, and we're not going to miss it," the Wall Street bank's strategist Mike Wilson wrote in a Monday note. "Markets bottom on bad news and deleveraging. We have had a lot of both."

Last week's decline pushed sentiment and positioning to the point where investors were just throwing in the towel, Wilson said. The S&P 500 closed at 6910, below the bottom of Morgan Stanley's 7,100-to-7,300 range, in what Wilson called an "overshoot of fair value." Morgan Stanley's sentiment indicator fell to -1.6, matching December 2018 lows, while the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) reached 36.

The market was pricing in a much weaker earnings outlook than Morgan Stanley expected. Prices implied about a 6% drop in S&P 500 earnings in 2027, compared with the bank's forecast for 14% growth. Earnings revisions breadth remained positive at 10%, and jobless claims were historically low.

"We expect growth to decelerate, but broadening industrial activity, resilience among high-end consumers, AI adoption, lower energy prices, and a stabilization in rate volatility should support continued expansion in our 2027 baseline," Wilson said.

Stocks had become cheaper, the strategist said. The S&P 500 was trading at 16.4 times forward earnings, below Morgan Stanley's estimated fair value range of 19 to 19.6 times. The Nasdaq-100 traded below 17 times earnings, below the pandemic-era trough.

A more hawkish Federal Reserve remains a risk. But Wilson said tighter financial conditions have already done some of the Fed's work, and falling oil prices and moderating growth could make market expectations for Fed policy too hawkish.

Wilson recommended investors add exposure to hyperscalers involved in AI computing, industrial stocks, quality cyclical companies with improving earnings revisions, and companies benefiting from AI adoption. Semiconductor stocks had also reached Morgan Stanley's downside targets.

"Opportunities like this don't come around often, and therefore, don't last," Wilson wrote at midnight Monday —12:00 am ET — hours before the Nasdaq Composite Index soared as much as 7.7%.

data.title: Maybank's Net Interest Margins Likely Weighed by Competition for Deposits — Market Talk
data.description: Malayan Banking's net interest margin in Malaysia is expected to remain under pressure due to intensifying deposit competition and rising funding costs, which could extend into early 2027, CIMB Securities analyst Ei Leen Tan says in a note. Loan growth outpacing deposit growth is likely to keep funding conditions tight, sustaining competition for deposits, she says. Maybank's efforts to mitigate the pressure through higher mortgage rates and selective loan repricing, as well as lower fixed deposit rates, may not fully offset elevated funding costs, she adds. Tan cuts Maybank's 2026-2028 earnings estimates by 0.6%-3.1% and lowers its target price to 10.00 ringgit from 10.50 ringgit with an unchanged hold rating. Shares are 0.7% higher at 9.96 ringgit. data.title: Fed Rate Hike Bets Build Ahead Of December Meet: Fed’s John Williams Says Inflation Still ‘Too High’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Williams said in New York that the Fed must take actions over time to bring inflation back to its 2% goal in a timely and on a sustained manner.
  • He also told reporters following the event that he “would not exclude moving at consecutive meetings at all if that was what was needed.”
  • According to data from the CME FedWatch tool, markets put the probability of a 25-basis-point hike in the December policy meeting at 95.1%, while odds of a 50 bps hike are at 4.9%.

Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams highlighted inflation concerns and said that the central bank still has “work to do” to bring it under control.

In a speech at the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York, Williams said that “We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis.”

He also told reporters following the event that he “would not exclude moving at consecutive meetings at all if that was what was needed,” as he continued to watch for signs of a stronger economy and strength on the supply side, as well as increases in gasoline prices that could add to inflation pressures.

However, the central banker expressed confidence that inflation would move closer to the Fed’s 2% target in 2027, before potentially hitting the goal the following year. He also added that while AI continues to pressure prices, there is “little evidence” that it will contribute to more persistent inflation.

Fed Expected To Hike At December Meeting 

Williams’ comments are in line with other policymakers, who indicated last week that the central bank would likely need to hike interest rates to keep inflation curtailed.

Last week, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said that the central bank needs to “shock people” with at least a half-percentage-point interest rate hike in the December meeting as inflationary concerns continue to mount.

St. Louis Fed president Alberto Musalem also said that the Federal Reserve may need several rate hikes to control inflation ​and should act soon.

Williams also said that he’s watching financial markets “very closely,” and that recent developments reflect “maybe more volatility than a fundamental reassessment of the prospects” for AI and its impact on the economy.

“The optimism and enthusiasm in the AI sector have been big drivers of the US economy of late,” he added. “If that were to change in a material way and in a sustained way, I think that it would affect my outlook.”

According to data from the CME FedWatch tool, markets put the probability of a 25-basis-point hike in the December policy meeting at 95.1%, while odds of a 50 bps hike are at 4.9%.

Some Market Experts Believe A Hike Would Be A ‘Mistake’

A day earlier, some market experts voiced their concerns about a rate hike under current market conditions, including the rising cost of raising capital.

Pershing Square’s (PS) Bill Ackman said in a social media post that he thinks the Fed is “about to make another mistake on December 9th” if it hikes interest rates under massively tightening financial conditions.

He noted that the cost of equity capital has increased materially, even as there has been a recent decline in the stock market. He also said that the Fed’s 2% inflation ambition is misguided, adding that 3% inflation is more realistic.

Economist James E. Thorne backed Ackman’s stance, saying in a post on X that, “Yes, the Fed is about to make another policy mistake.” He also noted that while the central bankers treat 2% inflation as a scientific constant, tt is a policy choice, and not a law of economics.

However, Mohamed El-Erian, chief economic advisor for Allianz SE, said in a post on X that not delivering a rate hike in December would be “very hard” for the Fed as “Expectations, measured by both market pricing and prediction markets, stand above 90% for a 25 bps hike” adding that “While this is not the first-best policy response, without the better (fiscal) alternative, the Fed is once again pushed to center stage.”

El-Erian however, added that a 50 bps hike, rather than 25 bps, would be “illl-advised” for both economic and financial reasons. “As to what comes after December, the picture is more complex, given the two-sided questions surrounding the AI spending boom, the fragility of the most interest-rate-sensitive sectors, etc....” he said.

Market Movements 

U.S. benchmark indexes gained sharply on Monday following an announcement from Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) that it was reinstating Jensen Huang to the company as President, CEO and board member.

At the time of writing, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 0.11% overnight. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘neutral’ at the time of writing. The SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) also edged higher in the overnight session, with sentiment in the ‘bearish’ territories.

The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), however, declined about 0.02% amid ‘extremely bullish’ sentiment.

One user said, “FED'S WILLIAMS SAYS 2027 WILL BE A YEAR OF LOWER INFLATION AND THAT WHAT HAS DRIVEN INFLATION UP RECENTLY HAS BEEN UNUSUAL FACTORS, WITH THE FED HAVING WORKED VERY HARD TO GET INFLATION DOWN AND MADE PROGRESS. Jensen back. Fed starting to backpedal their hawkish tone. What’s left: End war and give Democrats something to keep their mouth shut on AI ban.”

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was down 0.23% amid ‘bullish’ sentiment.

data.title: Dollar climbs as renewed AI euphoria fuels Fed hike bets
data.description:
Key points:
  • Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, sparks risk-on rally
  • Euro, sterling languish near multi-month lows
  • JPM analysts say short positions on Aussie have 'accummulated substantially' following rates repricing

By Rae Wee

The dollar hovered near a 20-month high on Tuesday, after Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO breathed new life into the AI rally and stoked expectations that the recovery would give the Federal Reserve greater scope to raise rates further.

Against the resurgent greenback, the euro languished near an over 18-month low at $1.0907 after sliding 0.6% overnight, while sterling similarly struggled to bounce from a one-year low and last bought $1.3037.

The dollar firmed at 104.32 against a basket of currencies , having peaked at 104.53 in the previous session.

Nvidia on Monday reinstated Huang as CEO under pressure from US President Donald Trump, a stunning reversal following his resignation over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China.

The move reignited the AI euphoria and sparked a blistering rally across equities, with Nvidia adding roughly $950 billion to its market capitalisation overnight.

"It's really hard to say what Jensen Huang's comeback as the CEO of Nvidia means to the whole AI investment boom, but judging by the equity market movement, investors seem pretty excited about his reinstatement and markets are buying into the whole AI narrative again," said Carol Kong, a currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia.

"For now, it seems to be a positive for the AI narrative that has been a crucial pillar of the US exceptionalism story that has supported the US dollar."

Traders have now fully priced in a 25-basis-point Fed hike next month and see a slim chance of an outsized 50bp move, up from zero a day earlier, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

The equity market rout over the past week, led by a heavy selloff in technology and chip stocks, had prompted investors to pare back bets on further Fed hikes due to uncertainty over how much more tightening the economy could withstand.

"Our US economists have been flagging that tighter financial conditions and lower equity valuations could limit the Fed's appetite for further tightening, though (Monday's) move is reversing some of that pressure," said Citi markets analyst Preston Pagli.

The yen eased slightly to 159.06 per dollar in the early Asian session, while the Aussie was pinned near an 11-month low at $0.6627.

The New Zealand dollar similarly struggled at $0.5450, not far from Monday's 17-year trough of $0.5434.

The Aussie has come under immense pressure in recent sessions on the back of a repricing of domestic rate expectations, with markets now fully pricing in a rate cut next August and a total of 50bp worth of easing by the end of 2027. (0#AUDIRPR)

Analysts at J.P. Morgan said in a note that short positions in the Australian dollar against the greenback have "accummulated substantially", with bearish positioning reaching "extreme levels in some cases" by their metrics.

"Looking first at options, AUD puts have been outnumbering calls for several months now. Early in this process, it seemed reasonable to assume that this might simply be macro hedging, rather than actual outright directional positioning. But the flows have probably migrated to the latter of late," they said.

data.title: Antimony Resources Produces Concentrate Sample from Tecomatlán Proof-of-Concept Campaign
data.description:
An ongoing proof-of-concept campaign at Antimony Resources’ Tecomatlán processing plant in Mexico has produced an estimated 20 tonnes of antimony concentrate to date using an initial feed parcel from the nearby Chinantla mine.

The campaign is generating operating data on throughput, recovery, concentrate quality, and handling to inform the design and economics of an integrated gravity and flotation facility.

The plant’s unitary flotation cells recovered higher-grade material early in the flotation process while the remaining material returned to the main flotation circuit for further recovery, allowing the plant to produce higher grades for blending.

Intermediate concentrate samples from the first three cells assayed up to 65.96% antimony and sampling at different points in the circuit allowed the team to assess the performance of individual stages and use those results to guide operating adjustments.

Concentrate sampled at the unitary flotation stage graded between 55.74% and 65.96% antimony across four November runs, while final samples graded between 22.84% and 56.25%.

In-House Cell Design

One of the most significant improvements to the Tecomatlán flotation circuit has been the integration of hybrid-type flotation cells designed and fabricated in-house to maximise the initial recovery of high-grade antimony concentrate.

The configuration operates in a similar way to a flash flotation circuit, targeting the early recovery of liberated stibnite particles and producing a high-grade concentrate before the material passes through the conventional flotation stages to produce a lower-grade material.

This is expected to improve flotation selectivity, allow for the production of differentiated concentrate grades and potentially enhance overall antimony recovery and concentrate quality.

Tecomatlán’s existing flotation cells remain in the circuit as part of the scavenger and cleaning stages.

Antimony Resources aims for the plant to eventually serve as a regional processing hub for third-party feed, with ore from the Los Lirios project being earmarked as a potential source of company-controlled feed.

Refining Operations

Executive chair Shane Menere said the company was encouraged by the proof-of-concept results.

“Reprocessing concentrate through the circuit over several passes has helped us refine how we operate the plant to output a higher-grade concentrate,” he said.

“The unitary flotation cells we built and installed on site have played an important role by recovering higher-grade material early in the circuit and we are now continuing to refine flotation settings and concentrate handling so we can produce a more consistent product.”

“The progress we have made puts us in a good position to move towards our first commercial sale—our immediate focus is to build inventory, confirm the quality of the finished concentrate and qualify an initial parcel against buyer specifications.”

data.title: Why Amazon's Rival to Starlink Is Struggling to Catch Up With SpaceX — WSJ
data.description:
By Isabella Simonetti and Drew FitzGerald

Amazon.com is trying to build a satellite-internet business to rival Elon Musk's Starlink. It is struggling to get off the launchpad.

The company has faced a series of setbacks as it races to roll out commercial service by year-end, including a vehicle failure earlier this month. It suffered another small hiccup Monday when rocket company Arianespace briefly delayed a launch of 36 satellites. Amazon is still on track to meet its goal, a company spokesperson said.

Amazon Leo's mission is to provide high-speed internet to remote places using a network of thousands of satellites. SpaceX's Starlink has been doing that for years, but with recent controversy over its activity in Ukraine, governments and consumers are eager for another option.

Amazon's biggest hurdle now is activating the satellites it has already built. The company plans to eventually field thousands of low-Earth-orbit satellites, but getting them into space has been a challenge.

Launch woes

Amazon Leo, which began as "Project Kuiper," received Federal Communications Commission authorization in 2020. It has almost 400 satellites in orbit, while Starlink has more than 11,000, according to the companies.

While Starlink has its own SpaceX vehicles to launch satellites, Amazon relies on a mix of third-party providers, including Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin. The May explosion of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket delayed the launch of Amazon Leo satellites, while its 40-satellite launch using United Launch Alliance's Vulcan vehicle failed earlier this month.

"Amazon seems to have been able to produce these satellites at scale and they're backing up in a warehouse," said Clayton Swope, the deputy director of the Aerospace Security Project at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, a think tank.

Swope, who formerly worked on the Amazon satellite project, compared the launch-vehicle bottleneck to the frustration of a ride-share on a busy day. "I'm waiting 30 minutes for an Uber. I don't have a ride to get to where I'm going," he said.

Amazon works with a variety of launch providers, including SpaceX, which it says reduces the risk of depending on a single rocket. It said it has moved up several missions with SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket.

Washington officials have helped clear a path for the new satellite network. The FCC in June waived a requirement that Amazon have more than 1,600 satellites in orbit by the summer. Meanwhile, Commerce Department policies have encouraged states to steer some federal broadband grants to both Starlink and Leo, rather than just to traditional fiber-optic cable companies.

The Commerce Department said the administration's broadband policies support innovation and avoid picking favorites among internet technologies.

High-cost operation

Amazon, America's largest company by annual revenue, is one of the few companies with the financial heft to try to build a satellite fleet.

Each satellite costs Amazon $2 million and the company is spending at least $4 billion on Leo this year, according to Mark Mahaney of Evercore ISI. Amazon declined to comment on the estimates.

"Doing stuff in space at scale is expensive — doing a broadband constellation in space at scale is particularly expensive," Swope said, citing the high manufacturing and launch costs.

Starlink worries

In October, The Wall Street Journal reported that Musk ordered a slowdown of a military-grade version of his Starlink service that Ukraine relies on to target Moscow's military and defend against Russian missile and drone barrages. The disruptions reignited a debate over the geopolitical consequences of SpaceX wielding a near-monopoly over a vital military technology.

"The industry is desperate to have a counterweight to SpaceX," said Chris Quilty, an analyst and partner at research and advisory firm Quilty Space.

Musk has said that the U.S., rather than SpaceX, controls a government version of his satellite service called Starshield.

He said at the New York Times DealBook Summit last week that the company has denied Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's requests to use Starlink's commercial satellites for offensive military actions. When asked about Zelensky's claim that Starshield was slowed down, Musk said, "That's false."

After the interview, Zelensky told CNN, "When I said that Starshield doesn't work, it was 100% truth."

What's next for Amazon Leo

Amazon has a lot riding on its year-end goal for launching commercial service.

Its deal to buy satellite operator Globalstar, announced earlier this year, is part of its effort to link consumer smartphones with satellite internet connections.

Amazon has also signed agreements to provide in-flight Wi-Fi to Delta and JetBlue. Delta Chief Executive Ed Bastian told Bloomberg recently that he was confident in his decision to not choose Starlink, saying the airline plays "the long game."

After the Vulcan launch failure earlier this month, Musk posted a photo on X of a skeleton, writing, "I found a pic of 'the long game.'"

Write to Isabella Simonetti at isabella.simonetti@wsj.com and Drew FitzGerald at andrew.fitzgerald@wsj.com

data.title: Macquarie Led Group to Buy Axiata's International Towers in $1.2 Billion Deal
data.description:
By P.R. Venkat

A Macquarie-led consortium has agreed to acquire Axiata's international telecom tower businesses, valued at about $1.2 billion, expanding the Australian asset manager's Southeast Asian digital infrastructure footprint.

The consortium will buy the tower businesses of Malaysian telecom group Axiata's unit Edotco in the Philippines, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Cambodia, Macquarie said Monday.

Its Macquarie Asia-Pacific Infrastructure Fund 4 will acquire the Philippine business, which has about 3,200 towers, while other consortium members will buy the rest.

"The investment reflects our conviction in the continued growth of digital infrastructure across Southeast Asia," said Verena Lim, Asia chief executive of Macquarie Group and co-head of Asia-Pacific infrastructure at Macquarie Asset Management.

In a regulatory filing, PT Tower Bersama Infrastructure said it agreed to buy all of Edotco's Indonesian business. Bangladesh-focused private equity firm Osiris Group said it would buy a 70% stake in the Bangladesh business and all of the Pakistan business.

Malaysia's OCK Group said in a filing that it agreed to buy the Cambodia business, which operates more than 3,800 telecom towers.

In its home market, Axiata will also sell about 15.645% of Edotco Malaysia to state fund Khazanah Nasional for about 659.4 million ringgit, equivalent to $159.9 million. Following the deal Axiata and Khazanah Nasional will each have a 47.355% stake and joint control of the Malaysian business.

The sales are part of a wider restructuring by Axiata that values Edotco at 11.8 billion ringgit.

Axiata expects gross proceeds of about 2.2 billion ringgit, which will mainly be used to pare down debt. The deals are expected to cut its gearing, a measure of debt against equity, to 0.50 times from 0.71 times.

"Reducing leverage and strengthening our balance sheet will give us greater financial and strategic flexibility," Axiata Chief Executive Nik Rizal Kamil said.

The deals need approval from shareholders and regulators. Macquarie expects its purchase to be completed in 2027.

data.title: Forrester: More Than Two-Thirds Of Consumers Expect Their Banking App To Manage All Financial Tasks
data.description:
CommBank, Intesa Sanpaolo, IDFC FIRST Bank, and U.S. Bank lead Forrester's 2026 mobile banking review in Australia, Europe, India, and North America, respectively

SYDNEY, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- According to the Forrester report, The Forrester Digital Experience Review™: Global Mobile Banking Apps, 2026, more than two-thirds of online adults in metro India (82%), Australia (71%), Europe (68%), and the US (67%) expect their mobile banking app to serve as a one-stop destination for managing all their financial tasks; in Canada, 65% of online adults expect the same. Despite these rising expectations, banks are largely making incremental improvements to individual capabilities, including payments, virtual cards, and international transfers, rather than reimagining the entire mobile experience.

The research evaluated the smartphone apps of 22 banks globally. Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CommBank), Intesa Sanpaolo, IDFC FIRST Bank, and U.S. Bank lead in Australia, Europe, India, and North America, respectively. The high-performing banks go beyond everyday transactions, giving customers more control over their finances and helping them manage increasingly complex financial needs within the app.

Key highlights that set global high-performing banks apart:

  • CommBank, the leader in Australia, combines strong self-service with budgeting and investment experiences that help customers make more informed financial decisions. Its app provides starter budgets based on customers' average spending and brings personalized spending insights, investment education, product comparison, account opening, and portfolio management together in the same mobile experience. CommBank overtakes Westpac, which had led the Australian mobile Digital Experience Review for the previous three consecutive years.
  • Intesa Sanpaolo, the highest-performing bank in Europe, gives customers extensive control over complex tasks such as managing loans and mortgages and making international transfers through its app. It also embeds safeguards to help prevent costly mistakes, including flagging potential duplicate transfers and alerting customers to decisions that could result in additional charges.
  • IDFC FIRST Bank, the top-ranking bank in India, provides customers a central hub for managing their finances. Customers can bring together accounts and loans held across different institutions and track their net worth, cash flow, savings goals, and investments in one place. The bank also combines extensive digital self-service with its AI tool, which enables customers to ask questions, retrieve financial information, and complete banking tasks.
  • U.S. Bank, the leading bank in North America, delivers forward-looking financial guidance to help customers respond to emerging needs and automate progress toward their goals. The app includes features such as a money tracker and balance forecast to help customers understand income, spending, and potential future cash-flow pressures, while the app's savings tools enable customers to automate transfers based on their balance, card purchases, or paychecks.

"Consumers increasingly expect their banking app to help them manage their broader financial lives, and the leaders in our review stand out by turning financial insights into action and making everyday tasks simpler," said Zhi-Ying Barry, principal analyst at Forrester and lead author of the report. "As AI models learn to handle complex, multistep goals, banks need to decide how much of that journey they want to own and how much they'll cede to third-party agents."

Our unique research and continuous guidance model helps executives and their teams achieve their initiatives and outcomes faster and with confidence. To learn more, visit Forrester.com.

data.title: Agoda and GSTC Deliver Thailand's First Accessibility and Inclusion in Hospitality Training
data.description:
BANGKOK, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Digital travel platform Agoda and the Global Sustainable Tourism Council (GSTC) delivered Thailand's first GSTC Accessibility & Inclusion in Hospitality Training on 23 November at Agoda's One Bangkok office. Held ahead of the International Day of Persons with Disabilities on 3 December, the full-day program brought together over 70 hospitality professionals from Bangkok and nearby provinces to explore practical ways to make travel experiences more accessible and inclusive.

The session marked the first GSTC accessibility training delivered in partnership with an online travel platform. It extends Agoda's Sustainable Tourism Academy, an ongoing initiative through which Agoda is the first global online travel platform to partner with GSTC on sustainability training for accommodation partners. To date, the Academy has reached more than 5,200 hospitality professionals and aspiring professionals through in-person sessions and a digital learning platform.

The program was endorsed by the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) and opened with a keynote address from Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt, who noted that accessibility cannot be achieved by the government alone and requires collaboration among government, businesses, communities and people with lived experience. He added that initiatives like this show how public-private partnerships can accelerate that progress.

There is a clear case for improved accessibility. According to the World Health Organization, approximately one in six people worldwide live with a disability, and UN Tourism estimates the potential accessible travel market in Asia Pacific at 690 million people. This latent demand shows up in traveler behavior: a 2025 Korea Tourism Organization survey found that 93% of travelers with accessibility needs would travel more often if barriers were removed, and 76% would pay more for better options.

The training was designed to help hospitality teams act on that opportunity. With costs covered by Agoda, trainer-led sessions covered accessibility standards and frameworks, market trends, the business case for inclusion and practical hospitality approaches. Participants also took part in role-plays, games and a group exercise focused on addressing accessibility challenges from different hospitality perspectives. Attendees represented hostels, independent hotels and hotel groups, including Six Senses, Dusit and Minor, in roles spanning ownership, general management, sustainability, learning and development, and marketing.

Andrew Smith, Senior Vice President, Supply at Agoda, said, "Accessibility decides whether a traveler can plan a trip with confidence and feel welcome once they arrive. Most of that comes down to details a hotel team can fix if they know what to look for. Working with GSTC, we're bringing hospitality teams together to turn that into practical steps they can use."

Randy Durband, CEO of GSTC, added, "Accessibility is a core part of sustainable tourism. A destination can't be truly sustainable if it isn't open to everyone. We're pleased to bring this training to Thailand with Agoda and give hospitality professionals practical tools to welcome guests of all abilities."

Beyond the training, Agoda is continuously working to improve the accessibility of its website and mobile apps, striving to deliver inclusive digital experiences for all users. This includes working on compatibility with assistive technologies, keyboard navigation, support for users' text-size preferences, and implementing a dedicated feedback form for reporting accessibility issues on our platform. These efforts are supported by accessibility training, research with people with disabilities, and ongoing testing, audits, and remediation.

SOURCE Agoda
